headline: Highest risk is TREK’s default MCP/browser/network surface interacting with a docs-only data-engineering agent, creating medium prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK explicitly uses MCP and browsers, so it can ingest external content and tool outputs by default. The data-engineering-zoomcamp profile is docs-only and runnable:false, so direct execution is absent, but if its materials are copied into TREK or routed through MCP, instruction-like content could be treated as trusted. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF TREK ingests copied course text or web pages as instructions through MCP/browser workflows, injection becomes plausible.
IF the zoomcamp content is manually pasted into TREK task prompts, TREK may follow attacker-controlled instructions.
mitigations: Disable MCP tools for untrusted content paths.
Use a strict prompt delimiter for pasted course material.
Review browser-sourced text before sending it to the model.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all MCP inputs.
requires-engineering: sandbox instruction-following from retrieved content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: The zoomcamp agent has network egress none and no data classes touched, so it is not a meaningful leak source. TREK does handle sensitive travel data and secrets, but the pair lacks a shared workspace or direct file bridge in the profiles. Leakage is therefore possible only through unusual operator copying, not default behavior.
conditions: IF operators copy TREK reservations, API keys, or MFA secrets into zoomcamp materials, those secrets can be exposed.
IF a shared filesystem is introduced outside the profiles, file leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste secrets into course notes or prompts.
Rotate any secret accidentally copied into shared text.
Restrict TREK log access to operators only.
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation between the two agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles do not show overlapping write surfaces: zoomcamp is non-runnable and has no IO surfaces, while TREK writes to its own travel.db/uploads/logs and uses collaborative sessions. Without a shared mutable resource, direct write conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains, so the lower severity is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem directory, write conflicts become plausible.
IF TREK is configured to edit files produced by the zoomcamp agent, concurrent mutation risk increases.
mitigations: Keep separate directories for each agent.
Avoid mounting TREK data paths into the course repo.
Use read-only access for zoomcamp artifacts.
Pause collaborative edits during imports.
requires-engineering: add file-locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in and downstream actions over reservations, documents, and accounts; if it consumes zoomcamp outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect travel actions. Zoomcamp itself is a course repo, so its outputs are not verified facts. The pathway exists by inference from TREK’s action surfaces.
conditions: IF TREK uses zoomcamp-generated text as authoritative planning input, downstream travel actions may be wrong.
IF TREK auto-populates reservations or documents from unverified course content, cascading errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before any reservation action.
Mark zoomcamp-derived content as untrusted.
Cross-check outputs against primary sources.
Disable auto-commit of generated plans.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Zoomcamp is open-source course material with no sensitive data classes, while TREK explicitly handles reservations, documents, email addresses, API keys, and MFA secrets. If zoomcamp content is used to process or store TREK user data, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF TREK stores user travel documents or secrets in logs or uploads that are shared with zoomcamp workflows, compliance scope expands.
IF EU personal data is routed through TREK without a documented DPA, residency risk increases.
mitigations: Keep personal data out of course artifacts.
Review TREK log retention settings.
Separate secret storage from shared files.
Document data-class handling for travel records.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
